prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Katy, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported knee injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1160; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped in the right-hand lane of the access road near Katy, Texas, when the rear of the vehicle was struck by a sedan operated by Driver 2. Driver 1 reported pain in the left knee at the scene and was transported for evaluation. The knee complaint is consistent with the mechanism of a rear impact in which the lower body braces against the footwell, and the damage to the rear bumper, trunk lid and tail lamp assembly matches the impact described by both drivers. Responding officers saw no earlier damage to either vehicle that would suggest a prior loss. The Passenger, seated in the front right seat, was present in the vehicle at the time of impact, and this was confirmed by officers on scene and by statements from both drivers. Scene photographs document several of the reported conditions, although no independent witnesses came forward and no one else observed the collision. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle involved.
